questions.prompt: Anthropic's guide says choosing a model means balancing three things. Which three?

options.explanation: Right. The guide says choosing a model means balancing capabilities, speed and cost. Its list of key criteria also adds effort.
None of these tell you whether the model fits your task.
A benchmark is not your task, and it ignores speed and cost.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's guide say to keep after you compare options?

options.text: The most powerful model, because it scores highest.
options.explanation: The guide points the other way: the lightest option that is good enough.

options.text: The lightest setting that meets your quality bar.
options.explanation: Right. That is the guide's advice.

questions.prompt: Why pin a production tool to a specific model version?

options.text: So its behaviour stays stable until you choose to upgrade.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's text guide recommends pinning to a model snapshot for consistent behaviour.

options.text: Because pinned models are free to run, while newer models cost more.
options.explanation: Pinning fixes the version. It does not change the price.

options.text: Because pinned models never hallucinate, as their answers are fixed.
options.explanation: Pinning only keeps the version stable. It does not make answers correct, so you still test and check them.
